You are doing functional research for "Atlas ERP", an open-source ERP whose explicit benchmark is SAP S/4HANA. Your assigned S/4HANA area: Controlling (CO).

TASK: Establish what this area actually covers in current S/4HANA (2025/2026), identify the 6-12 capabilities practitioners consider essential, and judge each against the planned Atlas v1 scope below.

METHOD: Use WebSearch (and WebFetch for promising pages) - 2 to 5 targeted searches. Prefer SAP Help Portal, SAP Community, and reputable ERP consulting sources. If web tools are unavailable or consistently fail, fall back to your embedded knowledge of S/4HANA and say so explicitly in the overview field.

COVER AT MINIMUM: Cost center accounting, profit center accounting, internal orders, product costing (CO-PC), margin analysis / profitability analysis (CO-PA), allocations and assessments, and how S/4HANA merged CO into the Universal Journal.

PLANNED ATLAS V1 SCOPE FOR THIS AREA (judge full/partial/out-of-scope against THIS, not your own ideas):
Journal lines carry cost center, profit center and project dimensions so all CO reporting is a projection of the universal journal; cost centers and profit centers with allocation rules; product costing fed by manufacturing (WIP journals, finish-to-stock); cost-center report and margin-by-product report generated from the ledger. Internal orders are not planned as a separate object (projects/WBS cover that role).

RULES:
- atlas_v1 = "full" when Atlas v1 plans the practitioner-essential core of the capability; "partial" when a meaningful but reduced subset is planned; "out-of-scope" when none of it is planned.
- Every "partial" and "out-of-scope" entry MUST have a non-empty reason (why cut / where the boundary sits) and later_path (how to add it later in one line).
- atlas_module must be one of: finance, inventory, procurement, sales, manufacturing, quality, maintenance, hr, projects, crm, reporting, admin, industry, core, frontend, or "-" for out-of-scope.
- Be honest: if S/4HANA has an essential capability the Atlas plan misses entirely, include it as out-of-scope rather than omitting it.

Your final output is consumed by a script - return only the structured data.

Based on the web search results, here's a comprehensive overview of SAP S/4HANA Controlling (CO) key capabilities:

## Key Capabilities of SAP S/4HANA Controlling (CO)

### Universal Journal Integration
In SAP S/4HANA, the Universal Journal (table ACDOCA) unifies FI and CO into a single stream of data, where every financial posting contains all the characteristics needed for both legal and management reporting in one line item. This enables real-time, integrated reporting without the need for lengthy reconciliation.

### Core Master Data Management
The Controlling module supports managing and configuring master data that covers cost elements, cost centers, profit centers, internal orders, and functional areas. Profit center assignment is critical, serving as the primary source for deriving the profit center in sales orders, production orders, and inventory postings.

### Organizational Structure
The Operating Concern represents the highest-level organizational unit in Margin Analysis (CO-PA), defining the structure for analyzing profitability by market segments, and can be assigned to multiple controlling areas. The Controlling Area is the central organizational unit in Controlling, representing a self-contained structure where costs and revenues are managed.

### Key Capabilities
The Controlling module manages and records all the costs and revenues that a company incurs, involving categorization of costs according to their nature and allocation to different cost objects.

SAP S/4HANA enhances traditional controlling features with real-time data processing and an improved user interface.

### Advanced Features
New features include universal parallel accounting and margin analysis for sales, customer projects, and services.

The Controlling module provides a toolkit for accurate cost accounting, perceptive profitability analysis, and rigorous internal reporting.

Based on the search results, here's comprehensive information about S/4HANA CO-PA margin analysis versus costing-based profitability analysis and their relationship to the Universal Journal (ACDOCA):

## Data Storage

In SAP S/4HANA, the account-based profitability analysis data and the margin analysis data are stored in the Universal Journal (table ACDOCA) in real time. In contrast, the costing-based profitability analysis documents aren't included in the Universal Journal, so the reconciliation of financial accounting with costing-based profitability analysis is a huge challenge.

## Margin Analysis (Account-Based CO-PA)

Margin analysis is fully integrated in the Universal Journal. It's therefore reconciled by design. S/4HANA Margin Analysis is fundamentally account-based, using GL accounts for all postings. However, it incorporates features from costing-based CO-PA, such as the ability to split COGS into its component parts (material cost, labor, overhead) for a more detailed contribution margin analysis.

## Costing-Based Profitability Analysis

Costing-based CO-PA groups revenues and costs according to value fields and applies costing-based valuation approaches. Data is recorded in a dedicated persistency apart from external accounting. There are no changes to the data model or in the set up and usage of the costing-based Profitability Analysis in SAP S/4HANA. SAP will not invest in the further development of the costing-based Profitability Analysis, but it is still supported for usage and implementation in SAP S/4HANA on premise.

## SAP's Recommendation

SAP recommends using Margin Analysis in SAP S/4HANA. Margin Analysis has been extended broadly over the past releases and we continue to conduct new developments in this area only. It is perfectly integrated into the overall concept of the Universal Journal and is therefore fully in line with our Financial Accounting development strategy.

## Overview of Universal Allocation in SAP S/4HANA

Universal Allocation has been a new SAP function for overhead cost allocation since S/4HANA 1909, developed to reduce the complexity of traditional allocation processes and offering a unified platform for the distribution of plan and actual data.

## Allocation Types and Context

The classic overhead allocation has been redefined as the assessment cycle, while available contexts are cost centers, profit centers, and margin analysis.

Distribution reallocates primary costs from one or more cost centers to other cost centers, while overhead allocations are similar to distributions for primary and secondary costs, using a secondary cost account with category 42 instead of the original G/L account.

## Fiori Applications

The SAP Fiori app Manage Allocation allows you to view a list of existing allocation cycles, and you can edit, create, copy, or delete actual and plan allocation cycles. Additional Fiori apps include Run Allocations for performing allocation runs and Allocation Results for displaying results of allocation runs.

## Key Benefits

Universal allocation in SAP S/4HANA streamlines what was once a fragmented and complex process in SAP Controlling, consolidating multiple allocation tools into one unified framework to reduce administrative overhead and increase transparency.

## Overview of Product Costing (CO-PC) in SAP S/4HANA

The variance calculation step analyzes the order balance and breaks it down into different categories, with the system categorizing the order balance into different variance types.

### Standard Cost Estimation and WIP

S/4HANA enables mastery of standard cost estimates, work in progress and variance calculations, reporting and analysis. The RA Version (always version 0 for actual costs) is the master control object that holds the parameters for how WIP and variances are calculated.

### Variance Calculation Process

Once an order is finished, SAP compares the planned costs to the actual costs to determine the variance, and the calculated WIP or variances are posted to the General Ledger (FI) and Profitability Analysis (CO-PA). Production variances are only split into Input Price Variance, Input Quantity Variance, and Resource Usage.

### Event-Based Production Accounting

Event-based production cost posting (including event-based WIP and event-based variance posting) is now available to calculate WIP and variance immediately instead of waiting for period-end closing, linking cost posting to business events, such as goods issues, goods receipts, and operation confirmations. As of SAP S/4HANA release 2022, event-based processing is available with the universal parallel accounting business function, where goods movements and confirmations trigger the overhead calculation, which triggers either the posting of a journal entry for the WIP or the cancellation of any existing WIP and the calculation of production variances.

### Settlement Process

The settlement of cost objects allocates the actual costs, WIP and variances to other cost objects or transfers them to P&L statement.

Based on the search results, here's what I found regarding SAP S/4HANA Cloud internal orders being replaced by projects:

## Deprecation of Internal Orders

New customers starting with release SAP S/4HANA Cloud 1905 will not be able to create internal orders. For existing customers internal orders app is planned to be deleted with SAP S/4HANA Cloud 2005. As of S/4HANA Cloud 1802, the internal order functionality has been removed.

## Replacement with Projects

The replacement for the Internal Orders function is called Project Financials Control. More broadly, Internal Orders are no longer the model SAP is designing for, and project-based structures built on SAP WBS elements are the default.

## Cost Collector Replacement

In a most simple scenario, an enterprise project has no project structure at all and simply acts as a cost collector, similar to an internal order in SAP S/4HANA On-premise or private cloud edition. Additionally, Instead of Internal Orders, in SAP S/4HANA Cloud, public edition we use WBS (Work Breakdown Structure).

## Key Difference

Internal Orders were built to collect costs. WBS elements are designed to control projects. For organizations managing capital projects or complex initiatives, SAP WBS elements provide greater control, visibility, and integration than Internal Orders.

input.overview: Findings are based on live web research (SAP Help Portal, SAP Community, SAP PRESS, and ERP consulting sources, June 2026). In current S/4HANA, Controlling is no longer a separate ledger world: FI and CO are merged into the Universal Journal (table ACDOCA), so every posting carries cost center, profit center, project/WBS, order, and profitability-segment dimensions, and all CO reporting is a real-time projection of that single table; cost elements have become G/L accounts. The practitioner-essential core comprises cost center accounting, profit center accounting, internal orders (deprecated in S/4HANA Cloud in favor of project cost collectors), product cost planning and cost object controlling (standard cost estimates, WIP, variance calculation, settlement, increasingly event-based), Margin Analysis (account-based CO-PA in the journal, replacing costing-based CO-PA), universal allocations (distribution/assessment/overhead), activity types with internal activity allocation, and cost center planning/budgeting, with Material Ledger actual costing as an optional deepening. Atlas v1's design — dimensions on journal lines, cost/profit centers with allocation rules, manufacturing-fed WIP and finish-to-stock, and ledger-projected cost-center and margin reports — matches the architectural core of S/4HANA CO and its cloud-edition direction (including replacing internal orders with projects), but leaves activity-rate machinery, planning/budgeting, variance decomposition, and multi-dimensional margin segments for later.

capabilities.capability: Universal Journal merge of FI and CO
capabilities.description: Single line-item table (ACDOCA) where every posting carries all CO dimensions; cost elements are G/L accounts; FI/CO reconciliation eliminated by design.
Cost center master data, primary cost capture on postings, secondary cost flows via allocations, and cost center actuals reporting.
Profit center derived onto every journal line, enabling management P&L and segment reporting by profit center directly from the Universal Journal.

Cost collectors for internal measures (marketing campaigns, small capex, events) with planning, budgeting/availability control, and settlement to receivers; deprecated in S/4HANA Cloud in favor of project cost collectors.
capabilities.reason: Atlas deliberately mirrors S/4HANA Cloud's 'Principle of One' by covering the cost-collector role with projects/WBS instead of a separate order object, but order-specific machinery (order types, statistical orders, settlement rules to cost centers/assets, budget availability control) is not stated in the plan.
capabilities.later_path: Extend projects with settlement rules, budget/availability control, and settlement-to-asset postings rather than introducing a separate order object.

capabilities.description: Cost rollup over BOM and routing producing standard cost estimates with cost component split, costing runs, and standard price release for inventory valuation.
capabilities.reason: Atlas plans manufacturing-fed product costing (actual costs, WIP, finish-to-stock valuation) but does not state a BOM/routing cost-rollup engine, cost component split, or standard price release/costing-run machinery.
capabilities.later_path: Add a cost-rollup service over BOM/routing data that produces standard costs with a component split, used to value finished-goods receipts and compute variances.

capabilities.description: Actual cost capture on production orders, WIP calculation, variance calculation by category, and settlement to stock/P&L/CO-PA; S/4HANA increasingly posts these event-based instead of at period-end.
capabilities.reason: Atlas plans the core flow — WIP journals and finish-to-stock postings, which matches S/4HANA's modern event-based direction — but variance decomposition (input price/quantity, resource usage, lot size), scrap analysis, and settlement profiles are not planned.
capabilities.later_path: Add variance categorization computed from journal deltas at order close, posting categorized variance lines to the ledger and the margin report.

capabilities.description: Account-based profitability by market segment (product, customer, region, channel) stored on Universal Journal lines, with COGS component split and attributed margin; replaces costing-based CO-PA, which SAP no longer develops.
capabilities.reason: Atlas plans a margin-by-product report projected from the ledger — the right account-based architecture — but only the product dimension; customer/region/channel segments, COGS split by cost component, top-down distribution, and realignments are not planned.
capabilities.later_path: Widen journal lines with additional market-segment attributes (customer, region, channel) derived at posting time and add segment-level margin reports over the same ledger projection.

capabilities.description: Rule-based periodic distribution and assessment cycles moving costs between cost centers, profit centers, and profitability segments; S/4HANA unifies these in the Universal Allocation framework with Fiori apps.
capabilities.reason: Atlas plans allocation rules on cost centers and profit centers posting through the journal, which is the practitioner-essential core; allocation to margin-analysis segments and plan-data allocation are the main S/4 extras not mentioned.
capabilities.later_path: Add margin-segment-context and plan-data allocation cycles on the same rule engine.

capabilities.capability: Activity types and internal activity allocation
capabilities.description: Activity type masters with planned rates (machine/labor hours) driving direct activity allocation and secondary cost flows from cost centers into production orders.
capabilities.reason: No activity-type master, rate planning/calculation, or rate-based secondary cost postings appear in the Atlas plan; production cost capture is implied to be direct journal entries without rate machinery, so conversion-cost absorption from cost centers has no planned mechanism.
capabilities.later_path: Add activity types with planned rates that generate secondary-cost journal lines from production confirmations, crediting the supplying cost center and debiting the order.

capabilities.description: Plan data on cost centers and other CO objects (table ACDOCP, Fiori import, SAC integration) enabling plan/actual variance reporting and plan allocations.
capabilities.reason: The Atlas v1 plan covers only actuals; no plan ledger, budget entry, or plan/actual comparison is mentioned, yet plan-versus-actual on cost centers is a core controlling activity for practitioners.
capabilities.later_path: Add a plan-line ledger parallel to the journal and extend the cost-center and margin reports with plan/actual/variance columns.

capabilities.description: Material Ledger is mandatory in S/4HANA for multi-currency/parallel inventory valuation; optional actual costing periodically revalues inventory and COGS at actual costs.
capabilities.reason: Not mentioned in the Atlas plan; actual costing is an optional deepening in S/4HANA (mandatory only as the multi-currency valuation substructure), so omitting it from v1 is a defensible cut.
capabilities.later_path: Add a periodic actual-cost roll-up job that recomputes inventory and COGS values from accumulated journal lines and posts revaluation entries.

content.text: Research complete. The structured assessment of S/4HANA Controlling against the Atlas v1 plan has been returned, covering 11 capabilities: the Universal Journal merge, cost center and profit center accounting, and allocations rated full; internal orders (via projects), product cost planning, cost object controlling, and margin analysis rated partial; and activity types, planning/budgeting, and Material Ledger actual costing rated out-of-scope.
